\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Matrix row span]
\lean{FABL.matrixRowSpan}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b003}
\label{FABL.matrixRowSpan}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
For a matrix $H$ with $m$ rows and $n$ columns over $\mathbb{F}_2$, its row span is the
subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ consisting of all linear combinations of its rows.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Row span as a generated subspace]
\lean{FABL.matrixRowSpan_eq_span_rows}
\label{FABL.matrixRowSpan_eq_span_rows}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.matrixRowSpan, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $m,n$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be an $m\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
The image of the linear map given by left multiplication by $H$ is the subspace of
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ spanned by the rows of $H$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Sum of selected matrix columns]
\lean{FABL.matrixColumnSum}
\label{FABL.matrixColumnSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $H$ be an $m$-by-$n$ matrix over $\mathbb F_2$, and let
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The sum of the columns of $H$ indexed by $S$ is the vector
in $\mathbb F_2^m$ whose $r$th coordinate is $\sum_{j\in S}H_{rj}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Support representation of matrix action]
\lean{FABL.matrixColumnSum_f₂Support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.matrixColumnSum, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $H$ be an $m\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb F_2$ and let $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$.
The sum of the columns of $H$ indexed by the support of $\gamma$ equals $H\gamma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Nonzero sums of small column sets]
\lean{FABL.HasNonzeroColumnSumsUpTo}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b003}
\label{FABL.HasNonzeroColumnSumsUpTo}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.matrixColumnSum, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $H$ be an $m$-by-$n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and let $k$ be a natural number.
Every nonempty set of at most $k$ columns of $H$ has nonzero sum.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonempty support criterion]
\lean{FABL.f₂Support_nonempty_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.f₂Support}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$. The set of
coordinates on which $\gamma$ is nonzero is nonempty if and only if $\gamma$ is not the
zero vector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dot product and matrix-vector multiplication]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProduct_vecMul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m,n$ be natural numbers, let $H$ be an $m\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb F_2$, and
take $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ and $y\in\mathbb F_2^m$. The dot product of $\gamma$ with
the row-vector product $yH$ equals the dot product of $H\gamma$ with $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Walsh character under matrix multiplication]
\lean{FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_vecMul}
\label{FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_vecMul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂DotProduct_vecMul, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_apply, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $m,n$ be natural numbers, let $H$ be an $m$-by-$n$ matrix over $\mathbb F_2$, let
$\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$, and let $y\in\mathbb F_2^m$. The Walsh character indexed by
$\gamma$, evaluated at the row-vector product $yH$, equals the Walsh character indexed
by the column-vector product $H\gamma$, evaluated at $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Matrix pushforward of a density]
\lean{FABL.matrixPushforwardDensity}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p155-b004}
\label{FABL.matrixPushforwardDensity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.pushforward, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $H$ be an $m$-by-$n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and let $\varphi$ be a probability
density on $\mathbb{F}_2^m$. The associated probability density on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is
the pushforward of $\varphi$ under the map sending a row vector $y$ to $yH$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient under a matrix pushforward]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_matrixPushforwardDensity}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_matrixPushforwardDensity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.pushforward_expectation, FABL.matrixPushforwardDensity, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_vecMul, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $H$ be an $m$-by-$n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$, let $\varphi$ be a probability
density on the $m$-dimensional binary cube, and let $\gamma$ be a point of the
$n$-dimensional binary cube. The vector Fourier coefficient of the density obtained by
pushing $\varphi$ forward under the map $y\mapsto yH$ equals the vector Fourier
coefficient of $\varphi$ at $H\gamma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier regularity of a matrix pushforward]
\lean{FABL.matrixPushforwardDensity_isApproximatelyKWiseIndependent}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p155-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p155-b005
}
\label{FABL.matrixPushforwardDensity_isApproximatelyKWiseIndependent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.HasNonzeroColumnSumsUpTo, FABL.IsLowDegreeFourierRegular, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.f₂Support_nonempty_iff, FABL.isLowDegreeFourierRegular_binaryFunctionOnSignCube_iff, FABL.matrixPushforwardDensity, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_matrixPushforwardDensity, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m,n$ be natural numbers, let $H$ be an $m\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and
let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb{F}_2^m$. Suppose that for every nonempty
set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|S|\le k$, the sum of the columns of $H$ indexed by
$S$ is nonzero, and that every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $\phi$ has absolute value
at most $\varepsilon$. Then every Fourier coefficient indexed by a nonempty set of at
most $k$ coordinates of the sign-cube function corresponding to the pushforward of
$\phi$ under $y\mapsto yH$ has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}
